name: remify
summary: Converts an absolute length to rem, against the root font size.

arguments.name: $value
accepts: an absolute length: px, pt, pc, in, cm, mm or q
a relative one such as em, rem or % is refused, since it has no fixed size

arguments.name: $root
accepts: the page's root font size, 16px by default
an absolute length, and not zero

caveats: `rem` is relative to the root, and the 16px this assumed could not be changed until 4.0.0. On a page that sets `html { font-size: 62.5% }`, a common trick for easy arithmetic, `remify(24px)` wrote `1.5rem`: measured in Chrome 152 and Firefox 156, that renders as 15px of padding rather than 24px, while `remify(24px, 10px)` renders 24px. Pass `$root` to say what the page's root is.

Any absolute length converts, not only pixels: Sass reduces `pt`, `pc`, `in`, `cm`, `mm` and `q` to the same scale, so `remify(18pt)` is the same as `remify(24px)`. All six used to be refused although each has one right answer. The relative units stay refused, because they have none.

`pixelify` converts back against the same 16px default, so `pixelify(remify(24px))` is `24px` again. That round trip holds for the default root only; a `$root` of your own has no matching argument there.
